name: visiting-hours-house-round5
title: Visiting Hours: the house, round 5 (the observatory tower, the crescent skylight, the garden-side windows, colours)
subtitle: Your notes on round 4: the garden-facing wall's tiny windows, the observatory's colour and shape ("more like a tower ... dark polished wood, or a dark stone"), a skylight worth using ("like a crescent"), the holes next to the door, and recolouring what the oxblood made clash (the ramp out of the kitchen). Grey = round 4, green = round 5. All tests pass (EditMode 912, PlayMode 154); a build passed smoke.
questions: The tower: dark stone (my pick: it reads as a different, older material than the clapboard) or dark polished wood?
Does the crescent read as a skylight you'd use (it's 2.6 m across, right over the telescope)?
The recolours: green sofa and armchair, navy blanket, mustard and teal rugs, ochre curtains, a walnut slide. Anything else that still clashes?
notes: The tower is 5 m across over the middle of the attic's west end; inside, its ceiling is 5 m up (a double jump fits under it); outside it stands 2.2 m taller (a lantern storey with tall windows under the slate roof).

The holes by the door were the wall's jambs flickering against the door frame (two faces in one plane): the frame now wraps them, and the outside walls no longer share a plane with the front wall anywhere.
Only the furniture's pink fabric was recoloured; its wood and pillows keep their colours.
